"The round has stalled"

Strategy

In short: a stalled round is a process fault or an evidence gap, and the pass reasons tell you which. Read them, fix the gap or pause, then compress what is left into two weeks.

Key points

  • Common faults: unlogged pass reasons, a dripping window, pitching top funds first, and slow diligence.
  • If three pass reasons match, that is the gap; decide whether it takes weeks or months to fix.
  • If months, pause the round, tell live funds why, and name a return date.
  • If no reason repeats, put every live conversation inside a two-week window with stated dates.
  • Do not widen the list to 400 names or drop the price in a panic.

This is operating guidance, not investment, legal or financial advice.

What it usually means

A stalled round looks like one thing from the inside. Meetings keep happening and nothing closes. From the outside, it is usually one of five faults.

The pass reasons were never logged. Three firms said no for the same reason, in slightly different words, and the founder heard three separate opinions. The pattern was there. Nobody wrote it down.

The window dripped. Outreach went out as introductions arrived, over months. No fund ever had to decide while another fund was deciding. Without overlap there is no urgency, and without urgency a maybe stays a maybe.

Tier 1 went first. The best-fit funds were pitched when the deck was weakest, as practice. They passed. The founder is now working the list from the wrong end.

Diligence waited on the founder. The data room was half-built. Each homework request took a week. Interest cooled while documents were assembled.

Or the gap is real. There is no organic evidence yet, and no process fixes that. The honest answer is to go and get the evidence, then come back.

Where it traces to

This traces to Part 4, with Part 3 behind it.

Part 4 said run the round like a sales process. Forty to sixty named funds, warm routes, a three-week window, a pipeline with pass reasons logged. Every fault above is a step from Part 4 that was skipped or done out of order. The round is not unlucky. It is unmanaged.

Part 3 said raise against evidence, not narrative. When pass reasons cluster around "too early" or "want to see traction", the round has not stalled. It has arrived at the evidence gap. Part 4 cannot close a round that Part 3 has not earned.

The first move this week

Read every pass. Not the summary you wrote at the time, the actual words. Email, call notes, whatever exists. Put each reason on one line in a sheet.

Pass reason, in their words Count Fixable this month?
"Want to see more customer evidence" 3 Only by selling
"Not our stage" 2 List fault, remove
"Team gap in go-to-market" 1 Possibly

If three reasons match, that is the gap. Decide in one sitting whether it can be fixed in weeks or needs months. If weeks, fix it and relaunch. If months, pause the round, tell the live funds why, and name the date you will return. Investors respect a clean pause more than a slow fade.

If no reason repeats, the fault is process. Compress. Take every live conversation and put it inside a two-week window. Tell each fund the date. Overlap creates the urgency the drip never did.

Finish the data room before the window opens. Then hold a rule: every homework answer goes back within 48 hours. Diligence should never wait on you.

What not to do

Do not widen the list to 400 names. More of the wrong funds produces more passes, not more offers. The list was sized in Part 4 for a reason.

Do not drop the price in a panic. If the gap is evidence, a lower price does not supply it. If the gap is process, the price was never the issue.

Do not keep "ongoing" conversations alive for months. Ask each one for a decision date. A fund that will not give one has passed and is being polite.

How you know it worked

Two signs. Every live fund has a stated decision date inside the next fourteen days. And the pass reason that clustered has stopped appearing in new conversations, because you fixed it or stopped pitching the funds who care about it.

The checklist

  • [ ] Every pass reason logged in the fund's own words, with a count
  • [ ] Remaining live conversations compressed into one two-week window with stated dates
  • [ ] Data room complete, and a 48-hour rule on every homework request

Common questions

What should I do when my fundraising round stalls?

Log every pass reason in the investor's own words. If reasons cluster, fix the gap or pause; if not, compress live conversations into a two-week window. This is operating guidance, not investment, legal or financial advice.

Should I lower my valuation if my round has stalled?

No. If the gap is evidence, a lower price does not supply it. If the gap is process, the price was never the issue.

How do I create urgency with investors?

Put every live conversation inside one two-week window and tell each fund the date. Overlap creates urgency that a drip of meetings never does.

How fast should founders respond to due diligence requests?

Finish the data room before the window opens, and return every homework answer within 48 hours.
